name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped
a generous pinch of each (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper)

writer_notes: Scaled to 14 servings at ~2.33x the source recipe; make_it directs the cook to split across two 13x9 dishes because 21 no-boil sheets (seven 3-sheet layers) will not cook through in a single pan.
Cottage cheese is intentional and load-bearing for the protein number; it is NOT ricotta. Do not let a regen swap it.
Parsley goes on the first two layers only, plus the garnish, per the source.
Chicken bites are breaded, which is part of the carb source alongside the noodles.
No cost_ps value or cost_lines were supplied in dispatch; prose uses the {{cost_ps}} token and makes no per-package cost-arithmetic claims.
Macro tokens {{cal}} and {{protein}} used in prose; locked band pass confirmed (496 cal, 40.7 g protein).

prose.intro_html: Lasagna has a reputation for being a weekend project you only tackle when you have nothing else going on. This one is not that. It leans on frozen breaded chicken bites, a jar of alfredo, and no-boil noodles, which means the oven does the patient work while you do almost none of it. Blend cottage cheese into the alfredo and you get a sauce that tastes rich but quietly hauls the protein up where we need it, right around {{protein}} grams a serving for {{cal}} calories. That is a full plate of comfort food that still fits inside a meal-prep plan, for about {{cost_ps}} a container. Warm, cheesy, and honest about the numbers. That is the whole pitch.
prose.shop_smart:
• The frozen breaded chicken bites are the anchor. Buy them by weight and bake or air fry straight from frozen. No thawing, no trimming, no raw-chicken cleanup on your counter.
  • Cottage cheese is the secret here, so do not swap it for anything else. Blended smooth it disappears into the alfredo and does the heavy lifting on protein. Grab it by the tub in whatever fat level your store stocks.
  • One jar of alfredo is plenty. A roasted garlic style adds the most flavor per spoonful, but any decent jarred alfredo works. This is not the place to spend up.
  • No-boil lasagna sheets save you a pot, a colander, and ten minutes of babysitting boiling water. Count your sheets before you build so you know you have enough for every layer.
  • For the cheese on top, grate your own parmesan off a wedge and shred the fresh mozzarella yourself. Pre-shredded is coated to keep it from clumping, and that coating fights the melt you want on a bubbling lasagna.
  • Fresh parsley is a small buy that earns its place. It only goes on the first two layers and the garnish, so a single bunch covers the whole batch.
prose.make_it:
Start by heating the oven to 425ºF. While it comes up, bake or air fry the breaded chicken bites according to their package, then roughly chop them into bite-size pieces. Next, blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, a generous pinch of salt, and the black pepper until it is completely smooth. That blended sauce is what makes this both creamy and high protein, so do not skip the blender.

Now build it. Because we scaled this up to feed fourteen, plan on two 13x9 dishes rather than trying to force it all into one. Spread a thin layer of sauce across the bottom of each dish so nothing sticks. Lay down 3 noodle sheets, then more sauce, then chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat the layers, but only use parsley on the first two layers, and finish the very top with mozzarella and parmesan and nothing else.

Cover the dishes and bake for 30 minutes. Then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges. Garnish with a little fresh parsley and grated parmesan, and let it rest at least 5 minutes before you slice it. That rest is not optional if you want clean squares instead of a landslide.
prose.portion_html: This batch makes fourteen servings, and the honest way to split a lasagna is to weigh it, not to eyeball it. Once your dishes have rested, set your empty container on the scale, zero it out, and weigh the total cooked lasagna. Divide that number by fourteen and you have your per-container target. Score the top into roughly fourteen squares as a starting guide, then lift the pieces into containers and even them out by weight so every lid closes on the same {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories. Corner pieces run a little cheesier and middle pieces a little saucier, so trading a bite between containers to hit the weight is normal and expected.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is the part that matters at the end of the week. A pan of chicken alfredo lasagna that tastes like a restaurant order lands at about {{cost_ps}} a serving when you build it yourself in a fourteen-container batch. That is the whole point of prepping ahead. You buy the tub, the jar, and the box once, you cook once, and the per-serving cost drops to something a takeout menu cannot touch. Comfort food does not have to be a splurge when you do the math before you shop.
prose.upsell_html: Cook it once, and lunch is handled for the better part of two weeks. If you want more prep-ahead dinners that eat like a treat but behave like a budget, the Thrifty Crew membership is a dollar a month, and it pays for itself the first time you skip a delivery order. Stack the wins, one honest container at a time.

head.description: High-protein chicken alfredo lasagna made with breaded chicken bites, blended cottage cheese alfredo, and no-boil noodles. A budget meal-prep dinner scaled to 14 servings at about 496 calories and 40 grams of protein each.
head.keywords: chicken alfredo lasagna, high protein lasagna, cottage cheese alfredo, meal prep lasagna, budget meal prep dinner, no boil lasagna, high protein meal prep, breaded chicken lasagna
steps: Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken bites according to the package directions, then roughly chop them into bite-size pieces.
Blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, salt, and black pepper until completely smooth.

Spread a thin layer of the blended sauce in each dish, then layer 3 noodle sheets, more sauce, chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat, using parsley only on the first two layers, and finish the top with mozzarella and parmesan. Split the batch across two 13x9 dishes.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated parmesan, then rest at least 5 minutes before slicing into 14 portions.
